_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: a mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so `s.stdio.semio.cad`'s oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.stdio.semio.cad` is a semio-NATIVE format, so its reference is a second IMPLEMENTATION written in another language from the committed grammars and the committed binary protocol rather than a third-party package.

oracles.rationale:
No third-party library in any ecosystem reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, so the second producer THE STANDARD requires is a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language. `../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-semio-cad/🐍️component.py` is that implementation: the `semio <envelope-id>.dsl v1` preamble and the `0x89 'S' 'E' 'M' 0D 0A 1A 0A` binary envelope, the whole `document = artifact-mark schema-line layers-line blocks-line entities-line` grammar in both directions - `layer`, `block`, `entity-record`, `point2` and the nine single-letter-tagged `entity` variants `L`/`A`/`C`/`E`/`P`/`T`/`I`/`S`/`D` included - the binary pack frame in both directions, and all sixteen verbs of this subset's vocabulary together with their inverses, written in Python from this subset's own committed snapshot grammar, binary protocol and mutations grammar plus the envelope section of the framework carrier module, importing nothing from and transliterating nothing of the Rust it judges. Two boundaries are recorded rather than smoothed over. First, the binary protocol document declares `layers`/`blocks`/`entities` one opaque trailing `payload` chain by its own admission, so that layer was DERIVED from the committed pack example's bytes - LEB128 varint counts, length-prefixed UTF-8 strings, little-endian `f64` coordinates, a `u8` bool and a per-variant `u8` entity tag in the grammar's own variant order - and the derivation is pinned by byte-exact re-encoding of that committed file, which a misreading could not produce; the layer `colorIndex` is written as a plain varint, which the committed drawing exercises only at non-negative values, so the Python refuses a negative one rather than guessing. Second, the grammars are silent on where an `add-` verb PLACES its addition, the implementation appends as the committed specification vectors do, and the consequence - undoing a non-final removal restores the value but not the position - is exercised at its edge by the feature rather than hidden: `mutate-remove-entity` removes the middle entity and `inverse-remove-entity` the final one. `package` is deliberately the empty string: the implementation needs no distribution, so it contributes nothing to the dependency ledger and nothing to the import-purity probe. The DXF route was surveyed again and still rejected on the merits rather than for absence - the oracle role may never link the subject crate, so `dxf` 0.6 could only be handed a drawing this repository's own exporter produced, and DXF's `BLOCKS` section carries no per-entity handle addressing that survives a write-read cycle, stranding the four `*-block-entity` kinds.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `semio-v1-cad-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 16-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

🖊️ THE BROAD CARRIER, AND THE ONLY ONE THAT WRITES. `SemioCadToDxf` maps layers, blocks (name, base point and nested entities) and all nine `CadEntity` variants, so DXF is the only carrier that can witness the layer, block and block-entity halves of this vocabulary at all — STEP reaches top-level Line and Circle geometry and nothing else.

The `dxf` crate reads AND writes, which is what makes the fixtures genuinely `third-party-generated`: every drawing in the `dxf-entities` family is assembled with the crate's own `Drawing`/`Entity` builders and written by its own `save_file`, so no byte of expected DXF originates in this repository. It knows nothing of `SemioCadSnapshot`; what it recovers from the bytes is an independent reading rather than our encoder agreeing with itself.

TWO MEASURED LIMITS, both recorded rather than smoothed over. First, this subset's dialect is r12 (`$ACADVER AC1009`) and the crate gates `ELLIPSE`, `LWPOLYLINE` and typed `DIMENSION` to R13+: a drawing built with them came back three entities short of what went in. Our own exporter smuggles Ellipse and Dimension through as bridge-owned RAW GROUP CODES (`DxfEntity::Other`), which is not standard R12 and which the crate does not recover as typed entities. The oracle's reach is therefore SEVEN of the nine entity shapes, and the two `*-layer` kinds carry an explicit uncarried requirement for the other two — our exporter additionally drops `rec.layer` entirely for those two variants, since neither `ellipse_to_other` nor `dimension_to_other` emits a layer group code. Second, `CadEntityRecord.handle` is never written by any arm of the exporter, so DXF entity identity is positional; a mutation that adds or removes one of two IDENTICAL entities is not distinguishable, and the corpus keeps its entities distinguishable on purpose rather than relying on an addressing the carrier does not have.

MEASURED, and this is what qualifies the registration rather than merely motivating it: the sixteen before/after pairs all report `carrierWitnessed: true` with non-zero difference counts (and exactly zero for `no-mutation`), while the `set-entity-geometry` gate separates a correct after-state from one wrong by 0.05 in radius and 0.1 in centre at `maxAbsoluteDelta` 0.000e+00 against 1.000e-01 — eleven orders of magnitude clear of the 1e-12 near-exact threshold.

📐️ THE SECOND CARRIER, ON A DIFFERENT ENGINE FAMILY FROM THE FIRST. `ruststep` is a nom-based structural Part-21 reader; the `dxf` crate is a group-code reader. They share no kernel, so where both witness a mutation the two readings check each other rather than one confirming its own parse.

A STRUCTURAL reader is the right shape here, and this was settled by measurement rather than preference. `SemioCadToStep` emits bare `CARTESIAN_POINT`/`DIRECTION`/`VECTOR`/`LINE` and `CARTESIAN_POINT`/`AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D`/`CIRCLE` records with no `PRODUCT`, no `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION` and no context entities. `brepjs` — the one STEP-capable package vendored in this repository, and the qualified oracle for the sibling `brep` subset — was run against a file in exactly that shape through the cc6 probe suite and returned `imported: 0`, because OCCT transfers shapes through product/shape-representation structure and there is nothing here to transfer; the same probe returns `imported: 1` on a committed `brep` fixture, so the negative is attributable to the content. Registering brepjs against this capability would have produced a probe reporting zero shapes on every cad fixture: a green capability standing on evidence never read. ruststep parses the identical file completely, resolving all seven entities, every `#N` reference and both `$` placeholders.

READ-ONLY, AND THE FIXTURE CLASS SAYS SO. ruststep's lib.rs advertises "reading and writing", but 0.4.0's write half does not reach text: `Record`, `DataSection` and `Exchange` all fail to compile in a `println!` because none implements `Display`, and `ast::ser::to_record` stops at an in-memory `Record` whose nesting disagrees with what its own parser produces for the same entity — `CARTESIAN_POINT` serialises to `List([String, Real, Real, Real])` where the parser yields `List([String, List([Real, Real, Real])])`. No third party in this repository can therefore WRITE STEP, so the `step-line-circle` fixtures are classed `handcrafted`, not `third-party-generated`. What ruststep contributes is verification: the generator reads every file back through it and refuses to emit one whose geometry it does not recover exactly.

SCOPE, honestly bounded: the step export leaf drops seven of the nine entity variants (`_ => {} // no B-rep/solid equivalent in this bridge's scope`) and never reads `from.layers` or `from.blocks` at all, so this oracle is registered against five kinds only — `no-mutation`, `set-snapshot`, `add-entity`, `remove-entity` and `set-entity-geometry` — and the probe returns `unsupported` rather than an empty `ok` whenever both sides read back identical. MEASURED: the same `set-entity-geometry` counterexample separates at `maxAbsoluteDelta` 0.000e+00 against 1.000e-01.

probes.rationale: An independent reader accepting the file at all, and reporting what it recovered. Nothing downstream means anything if the artifact does not parse.

comparisonProfiles.description: Two CAD artifacts compared as the ENTITY GRAPH a third-party reader recovers from them — layers by name/colour/linetype/visibility, blocks by name/base point/nested entities, entities by kind, layer, text and ordered geometry — never as bytes. Byte equality would fail on handle allocation and header ordering that carry no meaning; structural equality on the reader's own output is the operative question.

toleranceProfiles.description: 2D CAD entity geometry is recorded EXACTLY — points, radii and angles as f64, never tessellated — so unlike a solid there is no legitimate 'differently discretised but equally valid' reading of a LINE or a CIRCLE. The gate is therefore near-exact, mesh-shaped rather than brep-shaped, and the floor exists only to absorb f64 decimal round-tripping through the carrier's own text format. MEASURED: a correct after-state reads back at maxAbsoluteDelta 0.000e+00 while a circle wrong by 0.05 in radius reads back at 1.000e-01, so the gate has about eleven orders of magnitude of margin.

comparisonPipelines.description: The sixteen kinds of this vocabulary through the DXF carrier its exporter mints. DXF is the only carrier reaching layers, blocks and block entities, so it gates every kind; the two `*-layer` kinds additionally carry an uncarried requirement for the Ellipse and Dimension shapes, which r12 cannot express typed.

stages.description: An independent reader accepts the artifact and reports what it recovered.
The carrier actually encoded this mutation — a before/after pair that reads back identical is reported unsupported, not passed.
Near-exact structural agreement — the operative equality.
